text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page fired for `VPC-CP-UNREACHABLE` (sev: P1) — customer: AcmeRetail — 1845001234
alice (oncall): incoming page, acked. I'm grabbing it.
alice (oncall): quick summary: control plane for AcmeRetail's private deployment in us-west-2 showing connectivity drops to customer VPC. Agents reporting TLS handshake failures.
alice (oncall): impact: inference calls to Acme's private model returning 502/timeout for ~5% of requests, customers reporting increased latency. No data exfiltration indicated.
tom (eng-infra): thx. I'm checking control plane logs and agent heartbeats now.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alice (oncall) acknowledged the page — 1845001240
tom (eng-infra): seeing repeated `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` in control-plane -> agent mTLS logs. Possibly cert rotation issue.
jen (ops): rolling up to CS: @lee FYI, prepping customer comms. Any immediate workarounds we can offer?
lee (cs): on it — reaching out to Acme support channel to inform of brief interruptions. Ask if they can switch to hosted endpoint temporarily.
alice (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) validate cert bundle on control plane; 2) push hotfix to agent cert validation; 3) coordinate restart of agents in affected VPCs if needed. Tom can confirm.
tom (eng-infra): reproducing locally: control-plane cert shows CN=private-redwood, but Acme agents expect `acme-vpc-ca` chain. Looks like CA config didn't include customer root after last deploy.
alice (oncall): ugh, config drift. Did the config service rollout remove per-customer CA mapping? Any config change at 1844999000?
tom (eng-infra): check: config-deploy job at 1844999222 included an optimization for CA caching. I see a bug where empty entries overwrite per-vpc CA map. I'm preparing a rollback patch.
incident-bot: Deploy-bot: rollback PR queued — #3267 — triggered by tom — 1845001302
jen (ops): while rollback runs, can we flip control-plane to fallback TLS policy (allow legacy CA) for Acme only? That would avoid restart.
tom (eng-infra): yes we can enable `legacy_ca_allow` for vpc-id=acme-prod-1. Doing it via runtime flags now.
tom (eng-infra): command: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime-flags -d '{"vpc":"acme-prod-1","legacy_ca_allow":true}'` — applying.
incident-bot: control-plane: runtime flag applied to acme-prod-1 — 1845001330
alice (oncall): confirm: agents started reestablishing TLS sessions — I'm seeing heartbeats return for ~60% of nodes.
lee (cs): Acme confirms degradation improving, some clients still see 502s, but overall better. They've appreciated the quick patch.
alice (oncall): escalation note: if rollback PR merges and config job re-deploys, we need to ensure no other VPCs affected. Tom, can you include a strict migration test?
tom (eng-infra): PR updated with unit + e2e test that verifies CA map isn't clobbered. Rollback merge in progress.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalation to eng-sre (oncall) due to ongoing partial impact — 1845001400
alice (oncall): handing off — I'm moving to monitor for 30m post-rollback. @tom please own post-merge verification and postmortem. @jen please prepare incident timeline and customer note.
jen (ops): will prepare timeline. Draft snippet:
```
Summary: At 18:20 UTC, control plane rollout inadvertently cleared per-customer CA mappings, causing TLS handshake failures for private VPCs. Mitigation: applied runtime fallback and rolled back the config deploy. Status: restored for Acme; monitoring.
```
lee (cs): I'll send updated customer note with expected root cause and ETA for permanent fix.
alice (oncall): closing loop: last observed 502s dropped to <0.5% traffic. Setting last_message_ts to 1845001570 and marking page resolved tentative. Will reopen if regression.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident resolved? page cleared by alice (oncall) — 1845001570
